chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever breaks a part of the fast of Ramadan due to an excuse, then making it up consecutively is superior, and if he makes it up separately, it is good, there is no objection.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up missed Ramadan fasts if done separately versus consecutively?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility in Qada (making up) fasts when a valid excuse, such as illness or travel, prevents continuous fasting. It highlights the Shia juristic preference for consecutive makeup (Mutatabi') as superior (Afdal), yet validates scattered makeup (Mufarraq) as sufficient (Hasan), reflecting the practical ease granted to believers. This ruling underscores the balance between strict adherence to ritual form and the mercy of divine law in Shia fiqh.
